class.name: ParticleEffect3D
class.brief_description: Root of a reusable particle effect with per-emitter timing.

method.name: apply_collision_substeps
method.description: Raises the emitter's [member GPUParticles3D.fixed_fps] (up to 240) so that one simulation step moves a particle less than half of [param shell] plus its collision size. The speed is estimated from the process material.

method.name: clear_pool
method.description: Frees all pooled (finished, waiting) effects created by [method spawn] and [method prewarm].

method.name: clear_level_collision_cache
method.description: Frees the level collision bakes shared between effects. Call it when the static level geometry changes while the game runs, so the next effects bake the new shapes.

method.name: editor_preview_play
method.description: Plays the effect inside the editor (used by the Level editor's Preview Effect button), with particles colliding with the shared level collision of the edited scene. Animated values (light energy, decal opacity, sound pitch, emitter [member GPUParticles3D.fixed_fps] and [code]emitting[/code]) are restored when the preview ends, when [method editor_preview_stop] is called and before the scene is saved.

method.name: editor_preview_stop
method.description: Stops an editor preview started with [method editor_preview_play] and restores the authored values.

method.name: emitter_uses_collision
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] for a visible [GPUParticles3D] whose process material collides: [member ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode] is not disabled, or its shader reads [code]COLLIDED[/code].

method.name: get_pooled_count
method.description: Returns how many finished instances of [param scene] wait in the pool for [method spawn].

method.name: is_editor_previewing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while an editor preview started with [method editor_preview_play] is playing.

method.name: is_level_collision_ready
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the shared level collision (see [method prepare_level_collision]) of the world containing [param node_in_world] has finished baking.

method.name: get_active_effect_count
method.description: Returns how many effects are playing in the running game, counted against [member ProjectSettings.rendering/particle_effects/max_active_effects].

method.name: get_elapsed_time
method.description: Returns the time in seconds since the effect started playing, scaled by [member speed_scale].

method.name: get_emitter_delay
method.description: Returns the start delay of [param emitter] in seconds.

method.name: get_emitter_duration
method.description: Returns how long [param emitter] emits in seconds. [code]0[/code] means the emitter follows its own settings (one cycle for one-shot emitters, forever otherwise).

method.name: get_total_duration
method.description: Returns the time until every particle of the effect has died, or [code]-1[/code] if an emitter emits forever.

method.name: is_playing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the effect is playing.

method.name: play
method.description: Restarts every emitter and plays the effect from the beginning, honoring the emitter delays and durations.

method.name: restart
method.description: Same as [method play].

method.name: prewarm
method.description: Instantiates [param count] silent instances of [param scene] under [param parent] and puts them in the pool, so the next [method spawn] calls reuse them instead of instantiating (e.g. call it at level load for bullet impacts). Returns how many were created; at most 64 instances wait per scene.

method.name: prepare_level_collision
method.description: Bakes the static collision ([StaticBody3D] shapes and CSG with collision in the [param mask] layers) of the whole level under [param level_root] into shared [GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D] tiles on worker threads. The tiles are internal child nodes of [param level_root] (not saved) and serve every particle effect, so effects stop baking their own collision once [method is_level_collision_ready] is [code]true[/code]. The first effect with collision does this automatically while the game runs; call it when a level loads to have it ready before the first shot. Returns [code]false[/code] when no static collision was found.

method.name: seek
method.description: Restarts the effect and fast-forwards it to [param time] seconds, honoring emitter delays. Intended for editor scrubbing; the result is an approximation of the simulated state.

method.name: set_emitter_delay
method.description: Sets the start delay of [param emitter] in seconds. Stored as metadata on the emitter.

method.name: set_emitter_duration
method.description: Sets how long [param emitter] emits in seconds; [code]0[/code] uses the emitter's own behavior. Stored as metadata on the emitter.

method.name: spawn
method.description: Plays [param scene] (whose root must be a [ParticleEffect3D]) under [param parent] at the global [param transform] with [member auto_free] enabled. [param tint] and [param scale] multiply the effect's [member tint] and [member effect_scale] for this play only, so one blood effect can serve red and yellow blood and one explosion small and big blasts; a pooled instance played later without them looks as authored. A finished instance of the same scene waiting in the pool is reused (and moved to [param parent] if needed); otherwise the scene is instantiated. When the effect finishes it returns to the pool instead of being freed, and connections to [signal finished] made for this use are removed. See [method prewarm].

method.name: spawn_attached
method.description: Like [method spawn] (including [param tint] and [param scale]), but [param local_transform] is relative to [param parent] (for example a muzzle [Marker3D] on a weapon) and [member local_space] is enabled, so the effect and its particles follow the parent while it plays.

method.name: update_level_collision
method.description: Bakes the level collision around the effect now (see [member collide_with_level]). [method play] does this automatically; call it after moving a playing effect.

method.name: stop
method.description: Stops emitting new particles. Living particles finish their lifetime, then [signal finished] is emitted.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the effect frees itself after [signal finished] (only while the game runs).
If [code]true[/code], the effect plays when it enters the scene tree in a running game. Without autoplay its emitters stay silent until [method play] is called.

If [code]true[/code], emitters whose process material has collision enabled bounce off static level geometry while the game runs. GPU particles only collide with [GPUParticlesCollision3D] nodes, so when the effect plays it bakes the [StaticBody3D] (and CSG) collision shapes inside its emitters' [member GPUParticles3D.visibility_aabb] into a transient [GPUParticlesCollisionSDF3D]. The bake is limited to a narrow band around the faces and runs immediately (on a worker thread for very large geometry); it is shared by effects replayed at the same place. Characters and rigid bodies are left out. Emitters with collision also get a higher [member GPUParticles3D.fixed_fps] so fast particles do not pass through thin walls (see [method apply_collision_substeps]).

If greater than [code]0[/code], [method play] skips the effect when the current [Camera3D] is farther away: it emits [signal finished] on the next frame (and returns to its pool). A looping effect keeps checking every 0.5 seconds and starts once the camera comes closer. Effects with a [RadialDamage3D] event always play.

Multiplies the size of the effect when it plays in a running game: particle scale, initial velocity, gravity and accelerations, emission shape extents, [member GPUParticles3D.visibility_aabb] and collision size, light range, decal size and the radii of [CameraShake3D] and [RadialDamage3D] events. Lifetimes and timing stay unchanged. See [member tint].
The physics layers baked for [member collide_with_level].

If [code]true[/code], [method play] sets [code]local_coords[/code] on every emitter, so particles move with the effect. Use it for effects attached to moving nodes, such as muzzle flashes. See [method spawn_attached].
If [code]true[/code], a finite effect starts again when it finishes.

When [member ProjectSettings.rendering/particle_effects/max_active_effects] effects are already playing, [method play] cuts off the oldest playing effect with the lowest priority not above this one. If every playing effect has a higher priority, this effect is skipped like with [member cull_distance]. Effects with a pending [RadialDamage3D] event are never cut off or skipped.

Multiplies the color of the emitters (the process material or CPU [code]color[/code], which also tints color ramps), the [code]light_color[/code] of lights and the color of decals when the effect plays in a running game. The values are applied in [method play] on local copies of the process materials, so shared resources are not changed; the authored values are remembered on the nodes, and a play with white tint and [member effect_scale] [code]1.0[/code] restores them. The editor always shows the authored effect.
Scales the effect timeline (delays and durations). It does not change the emitters' own simulation speed.

signal.name: finished
signal.description: Emitted when every emitter has stopped and all particles have died, or after [method stop] once the remaining particles are gone.
